status.name: Concentration
entries: Some powers require you to maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} in order to keep their effect active. If you lose {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}, such a power ends.

If a power must be maintained with {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}, that fact appears in its Duration entry, and the power specifies how long you can concentrate on it. You can end {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} at any time (no action required).

Normal activity, such as moving and attacking, doesn't interfere with {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}. The following factors can break {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}:
- Casting another power that requires {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}. You can't concentrate on two powers at once.

- Taking damage. Whenever you take damage while concentrating on a power, you must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}. The DC equals 10 or half the damage you take, whichever number is higher. If you take damage from multiple sources, such as an arrow and a dragon's breath, you make a separate {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} for each source of damage.

- Being {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or killed. You lose {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} on a power if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or if you die.
